notes: No project precedent (first EQ3 extraction). ACCESS: robots.txt checked FIRST -- no Claude-specific disallow (no ClaudeBot / Claude-User / Claude-SearchBot / Claude-Web / anthropic tokens; only Pinterest crawl-delays and standard account/cart/checkout/_next-static disallows), so clear to proceed. Plain direct fetch (desktop Chrome UA) returned HTTP 200 on robots.txt, sitemap.xml and every category page -- no WAF/challenge, no Rule 2 escalation needed for the storefront. LOCALE: robots.txt confirms eq3.com splits into /ca/en/, /ca/fr/ and /us/en/. The roster lists Canada so the ENGLISH CANADIAN storefront (/ca/en/) was used throughout, and every link below is a /ca/en/ URL. A US split does exist and is MATERIAL, not cosmetic -- spot-checked three nodes: Mirrors CA 13 vs US 8, Pendant Lamps CA 75 vs US 57, Decoration CA 29 vs US 16. The Canadian catalogue is consistently the larger one; had /us/en been used the qty would have been wrong on every row. PLATFORM: Next.js SSR app. api.eq3.com (the XHR backend, POST /product-instance/search) is hard-403 to every access route tried -- plain curl with Origin/Referer/X-EQ3-DeviceId headers, and a 10-profile curl_cffi impersonation sweep (chrome131/124/120/116/110/107, edge101, safari17_0/15_5, firefox133) all returned 403, so the API was NOT usable. Side door used instead per Rule 2: the server-rendered __NEXT_DATA__ blob on each category page embeds the React-Query dehydrated state including the full /product-instance/search response -- its own "count" field plus the product objects. STALE-SITEMAP TRAP (important): sitemap.xml is out of date and lists retired nodes. Slugs /category/lighting/lighting/*, /category/outdoor/*, /category/rugs/* and /accents/sculptures-wall-art no longer resolve -- their SSR query silently falls back to a parameterless catalogue-wide search returning count=1066 (the entire site) or to the bare parent subcategory. Taking those numbers at face value would have produced grossly inflated qty. The site's OWN live nav (the /site-navigation/menu-summary payload: 10 categories, 36 subcategories, 140 product lines) was used as the authoritative taxonomy instead, which shows Lighting and Rugs are now SUBCATEGORIES under Accessories (/category/accessories/lighting/... , note the live slug is lowercase 'table-and-desk-lamps'), that Outdoor and Sculptures & Wall Art are retired outright, and that the sitemap itself is only partial (it lists 3 mirror products against a true count of 13), so the sitemap was rejected as a counting source. COUNT VERIFICATION (Rule 1): every qty below is EXHAUSTION-VERIFIED, not a bare trust of the platform total. The category route accepts a ?page=N query param that makes the SSR prefetch N pages of 24 products; for every node with count>24 the page was re-fetched at ceil(count/24)+1 -- deliberately one page PAST the boundary -- and the unique product IDs harvested from the payload were counted. Unique-ID count equalled the reported count on 25 of 25 nodes tested, with zero mismatches, so EQ3's count field is exact here (contrary to the Shopify/Magento inflation pattern seen elsewhere on this project). Nodes with count<=24 are self-verifying since the first SSR page returns the whole set. RULE 0 GAINS: Lighting is buried as a subcategory of Accessories, not a top-level node, and was reached only via the live nav after the sitemap's /lighting/lighting/* path proved retired -- all 4 fixture lines (163 rows, 159 unique products) recovered. All mirrors included. EXCLUSIONS with titles actually inspected: Organization (14 -- Nomad/Prana/Trundle/Scoop/Climb/Leo baskets, Station Magazine Rack, Stak Containers, Duo Shelf: storage roll-up, dropped not padded); Bathroom Accessories (11 -- mixed roll-up: Trickle Shower Curtain and Silk & Snow Terry Bathmat are textiles, 3 Solid Teak Stools are furniture, Orb Wood Knob is hardware, Stak Containers is storage, and its only 4 genuinely decorative items are Spy Rectangle Mirror + the 3 Puddle Mirrors which are ALREADY counted inside Mirrors -- verified by product-ID intersection, 4 of 11 shared with Mirrors -- so it contributes zero unique in-scope product and was dropped rather than padded); Shelves & Hooks (3 -- Harvest Art Ledges and Duo Shelf are shelving, Orb Wood Knob is hardware); Kitchen Accessories (4 -- Pog Oak Boards, Bear Coffee Scoop, Mai Cast Iron Trivet, Merino Carafe Set: kitchenware); Bar Accessories (3 -- Crescent Ice Scoop/Ice Bucket/Wine Cooler: bar tools); Wine Racks (0, empty and out of scope anyway); Flatware (cutlery); Bulbs (explicitly excluded by Rule 0.2); Accent Pillows, Throw Blankets, Fabrics, Kitchen & Table Linens, all Rugs and all bedding (textiles); every furniture line across Living/Dining/Bedroom/Office; and Best Sellers, Gifts, Inspiration, Collections, Trending, Bestsellers and Sale as NEVER-EXTRACT nodes. Candles & Holders was kept after reading titles -- its 2 entries are Plinth Candle Holder variants, i.e. holders, with no scented candles present. BRAND-RECUT DETERMINATION (Rule 0.6 / brand-listing rule): the Brands tree (/category/eq3plus/) includes a full Kuzco Lighting sub-tree (Pendants 31, Chandeliers 22, Table Lamps 19, Floor Lamps 3, Wall Lights 23, Flush & Semi-Flush Mounts 12 = 108 unique). These are brand/designer listing pages, which the brief lists under NEVER EXTRACT, and product-ID intersection confirms they are substantially a brand re-cut of EQ3's own lighting tree: 72 of those 108 products (67 percent) already appear in /accessories/lighting/*. The whole Brands branch (Kuzco Lighting, Branch, Silk & Snow, Au Lit, More Brands/Tala) was therefore excluded and no Kuzco row is emitted. Flagging the residue for transparency: 36 Kuzco products (mostly chandeliers and flush/semi-flush mounts, fixture types EQ3's own 4-line lighting tree has no node for) are NOT reachable from /accessories/lighting/, so this exclusion is slightly conservative on lighting coverage. RULE 0.6 INTERNAL OVERLAP (documented, both nodes emitted): within the Accents subcategory the site cross-lists a product into more than one product line. Decoration and Vases & Plant Pots share 15 IDs but neither is a subset of the other (14 unique to each side), so both are genuine product lines and both are emitted; Decoration also shares 9 IDs with the excluded Organization node and 1 with Dinnerware. Inside Lighting, Pendant Lamps and Wall Lamps share 2 IDs and Floor Lamps and Table & Desk Lamps share 2, so the 4 lighting leaves sum to 163 but cover 159 unique products. Leaf qty values are left as the site's own per-node counts and are deliberately NOT deduplicated against each other, per the exact-count rule. The Accents subcategory as a whole reports 100 products, an independent cross-check consistent with this cross-listing. Every one of the 13 leaf rows carries a verified integer qty -- no nulls, no MANUAL REVIEW flags -- hence status ok.
